answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity like pigment traded in a canyon market: every new agent must stake a small, non-refundable deposit that is released slowly only as it completes verified work, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive while honest ones earn the stake back. Reputation then spreads like a river delta, flowing outward from a few anchored, high-stake agents through attested transactions, and an agent with no history or stake simply cannot reach the valuable flows. The cost is the filter, not a permission list.
